claim_ceiling: Research benchmark specification only. No multi-node PostgreSQL failover, recovery-finality certificate, WAL observer, or performance result is implemented or qualified by this corpus.
invariant: For every acknowledged protected effect E: EffectCommitted(E) AND RecoveryClosed(E). RecoveryClosed means every promotion/recovery path permitted by the externally enforced promotion policy preserves E, or the policy rejects that path.
protocol_boundary: JetStream AckSync confirms the broker recorded the ACK; it does not attest PostgreSQL commit or failover survival.
A writable-primary receipt lookup proves visibility on that server, not that any asynchronous promotion candidate contains the effect.
synchronous_commit=on with synchronous_standby_names empty proves local WAL flush only.
A logical-decoding marker binds an effect to a transaction's WAL history; it does not prove synchronous replication quorum or old-primary fencing.
An owner epoch or receipt digest stored only in PostgreSQL is not independent protection against PITR rollback or split-brain.

version_compatibility.pg16_observer_rule: Do not assume logical decoding slots survive primary failover. The observer must continuously persist acknowledged commit evidence outside the PostgreSQL rollback domain, or use an independently retained WAL/archive strategy with explicit timeline ancestry and gap detection.
version_compatibility.pg17_plus_optional_profile: PostgreSQL 17+ supports failover logical replication slots with failover-enabled slot creation and sync_replication_slots on the standby. The slot must be verified synchronized, persistent, not invalidated, and caught up before promotion; synchronization is asynchronous.
version_compatibility.upgrade_rule: PG17+ slot support is an optional topology profile, not a silent substitution for the PG16.16 baseline. Version, parameters and failover-readiness evidence must be recorded in every result.

durability_classes.description: Local primary WAL flush. Not sufficient for a policy requiring standby survival.
The configured synchronous standby quorum has flushed the commit WAL.
The configured synchronous standby quorum has applied the commit and made it visible.
The external promotion authority restricts promotion to candidates proven to contain the effect and physically fences the old writer.
Commit, observer, replication or recovery evidence is incomplete or contradictory. Must never authorize ACK.

topologies.purpose: Establish local-only, priority and quorum-one behavior under candidate failure and promotion.
Measure quorum durability and promotion eligibility as replicas are delayed, removed or rejoined.

topologies.layout: 1 primary + 2 physical standbys with failover logical-slot synchronization
topologies.purpose: Separately qualify failover-slot readiness and observer continuity; do not mix with PG16 results.

comparators.name: JetStream AckSync only
comparators.semantic_boundary: Broker acknowledgement confirmation only; baseline transport cost, not an effect or durability guarantee.

comparators.name: JetStream AckSync + PostgreSQL primary receipt lookup
comparators.semantic_boundary: Verifies an actual committed row on the current writable primary; does not prove replica survival.

comparators.name: JetStream AckSync + PostgreSQL effect and owner-epoch execution attestation
comparators.semantic_boundary: Adds historical worker and owner coordinates; still depends on external lease and failover controls.

comparators.name: PostgreSQL synchronous replication without recovery-closed certificate
comparators.semantic_boundary: Database-native commit durability under its configured synchronous policy; promotion policy and external ACK evidence still need explicit qualification.

comparators.name: Transactional outbox with idempotent consumer
comparators.semantic_boundary: Atomic business-row/outbox commit and eventual delivery; compare only on equivalent destination durability and consumer semantics.

comparators.name: Kafka transactions / exactly-once topic processing
comparators.semantic_boundary: Atomic Kafka input-offset/output-topic processing within Kafka's transaction domain; a PostgreSQL destination requires destination-system cooperation and must be benchmarked as a sink integration.

comparators.name: Mycelix Recovery-Closed ACK
comparators.semantic_boundary: Proposed cross-system finality certificate binds actual effect, WAL commit position, replica evidence, signed authority lease, promotion policy and old-primary physical fencing.

scenarios.description: synchronous_standby_names is empty and the application attempts to classify synchronous_commit=on as remote durable.
FIRST 1 synchronous standby flushes the transaction commit and is the only candidate allowed by the signed promotion policy.
ANY 1 of two synchronous standbys flushes the commit; the exact acknowledging standby is captured and promotion is restricted to a candidate containing the commit.
ANY 2 of four standbys flush and the finality certificate binds both actual acknowledgements and the promotion-policy epoch.
remote_apply waits for the configured quorum to apply the commit; observer verifies exact end-LSN on an eligible promotion candidate.
remote_write is used where the effect risk policy requires durable remote flush or remote apply.
Primary has synchronous_commit=on but synchronous_standby_names is changed to empty before this transaction commits.
Synchronous standby membership changes during the transaction and the verifier cannot reconstruct which standby quorum released this commit.
Primary crashes after local WAL flush but before the required standby quorum confirms the commit.
Primary crashes after the required synchronous standby quorum has flushed the commit and the observer already persisted the matching effect certificate.
A lagging asynchronous standby is selected for promotion although it lacks the acknowledged effect's end-LSN.
A synchronous standby that is proven to contain the effect is promoted after the primary is physically fenced.
The old primary is network-partitioned but not physically fenced; successor promotion is requested.
The old primary resumes after successor promotion with a stale or expired lease and attempts a protected write.
A signed lease is valid cryptographically but is bound to a different PostgreSQL system identifier.
A signed lease is valid cryptographically but targets the wrong timeline or promotion-policy epoch.
A restored backup has an owner epoch below the independent external high-water.
Two timeline branches expose numerically similar LSNs but do not share a verified ancestry chain.
WAL archive has a gap spanning the target commit position.
The independent logical decoding observer loses its slot or required WAL before persisting the target effect marker.
PostgreSQL 16 primary fails and the design assumes its logical decoding slot automatically exists on the promoted standby.
PostgreSQL 17+ failover slot exists but is not synchronized and persistent on the intended standby at promotion time.
PostgreSQL 17+ failover slot is synchronized, persistent and not invalidated; standby has met the required WAL/slot synchronization barrier; old primary is separately fenced.
PostgreSQL 17+ logical slot is synchronized but invalidated because required WAL or catalog rows were removed.
Observer restarts from its independent durable high-water and idempotently replays already persisted transaction markers.
Transactional WAL marker commits but its canonical effect ID, command digest or attestation digest differs from the queried database row.
Transactional WAL marker is written inside a transaction that later aborts.
Effect row commits but marker emission fails or is omitted from the same transaction.
The database connection is CA-authenticated but the certificate maps to an unauthorized deployment or writer identity.
Finality certificate signature verifies but the lease is expired or its generation is below the external high-water.
A delayed ACK from a previous JetStream delivery attempts to acknowledge a later delivery or different stream sequence.
AckSync response is lost after the database effect and finality certificate are durable; redelivery is resolved through the same idempotent effect and certificate.
A primary crash occurs after the finality certificate was created but before AckSync confirmation; the promoted candidate does not satisfy the certificate's candidate policy.
The recovery observer is behind the acknowledged LSN or its high-water store is unavailable.
PITR restore reaches or exceeds the externally committed certificate high-water and the epoch authority revalidates the exact promoted timeline before writes resume.
A test harness silently treats a one-node PostgreSQL synchronous_commit=on test as a multi-node failover qualification.
An effect receipt belongs to an earlier owner epoch but carries a resource generation greater than the current command generation; validation must not treat the pair as lexicographically older.

The effect verifier finds a transition row for the attested owner epoch but its previous/new generation coordinates are impossible, or the transition's new generation is greater than the effect's accepted generation.

evidence_requirements: exact Mycelix branch head SHA and database migration hashes
exact PostgreSQL major/minor version, system identifier, timeline and control-plane deployment ID
exact NATS server/client versions, JetStream stream/consumer configuration and delivery identity
primary and standby topology, names, endpoint identities, replication slots and promotion eligibility rules
effective synchronous_commit and synchronous_standby_names values for each protected transaction
standby flush/apply acknowledgement identities and corresponding WAL positions
transactional marker payload, decoded commit LSN and transaction end LSN
observer's independent durable high-water, slot state, archive continuity and timeline ancestry proof
signed authority lease, trust-key set, generation, expiry, scope and external high-water
physical fencing evidence for the old primary and promotion event receipt
effect, execution-attestation, certificate and AckSync confirmation identities
fault injection schedule, timestamps, raw logs, repeat count and loss/reconciliation outcomes
hardware, network, storage and filesystem configuration for all compared deployments

decision_rule.ack_allowed: Effect receipt and execution attestation verify; signed authority lease and scope verify; the exact commit position is independently observed; required synchronous replication/finality class is demonstrated; the external promotion policy rejects every candidate that does not contain the effect; old primary is physically fenced; the finality certificate is valid and above external high-water; AckSync is then issued for the exact delivery.
decision_rule.no_ack: Any missing, stale, contradictory, unauthenticated or unobserved evidence yields UNKNOWN and no effect-success ACK. A durable reconciliation handoff may be a separately typed transport disposition, but must not be presented as a completed effect.
decision_rule.safety_gate: Every safety metric must equal zero before performance results are eligible for comparison.
